title: Fix completion before accuracy
statement: Measure how much of the intended work learners actually finish before tuning accuracy or redesigning content, and when completion is low, fix it and size the course to it first.
example: The course one reading project set out to improve had a median completion of 12.5%.
detail: One redesign of a reading course led with daily 25-minute doses and put completion mechanics before accuracy lifts, noting a cohort floor of 12.5% (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0007-ti-courseplans-repo.qmd`). A later summary of the project's direction calls completion the first problem: the course it set out to improve had a median completion of 12.5%, with about 30% of the intended work done (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0217-team-direction-2026-09-09.qmd`).
against: Completing work is not learning, and nothing here shows that fixing completion first raised accuracy. Completion is necessary, not sufficient: the planning record calls dosage necessary-not-sufficient and pairs every completion claim with an accuracy measure on the same students (`grade3-reading/artifacts/GOAL_grade3_hootl_convergence_2026_06_15.md`). The 83% accuracy beside the completion figures was a blend heavily weighted by easier item types (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/approval_clean.md`), later corrected as the wrong instrument (`grade3-reading/artifacts/team-direction-2026-09-09/DIRECTION-2026-09-09.md`), so accuracy may bind too. The length rests on one course, and the review left the choice between 98 lessons and 48 to 60 to a group decision. the proposals agreed on the problem but weighed it differently: four made it the primary design constraint, two treated it as an input, and one underweighted it (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0244-g3-proposal-bakeoff-seven-proposals-2026-06-15.qmd`, lines 111-112).
